description.value: The study examined age-related differences in ACC functional connectivity during cognitive emotion regulation using psychophysiological interaction analyses in younger and older adults.
A cross-sectional study of younger and older healthy adults performing emotion-regulation conditions during fMRI.

spans.text: Functional connectivity with the ACC was compared when younger (18–35) and older (55–85) adults
Separate PPI analyses were conducted for younger and older adults.
Reappraisal > passive viewing: young adults |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

definition.value: When comparing reappraisal to passive viewing, functional connectivity was stronger for the reappraisal condition within several PFC regions.

value: For younger adults, significantly stronger connectivity with the ACC was observed in the reappraisal relative to the passive viewing and selective attention conditions. When comparing reappraisal to passive viewing, functional connectivity was stronger for the reappraisal condition within several PFC regions, including left DLPFC and left ventrolateral PFC (VLPFC).

spans.text: Reappraisal > selective attention: young adults |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

definition.value: Functional connectivity was stronger for reappraisal than selective attention in young adults.

value: For younger adults, significantly stronger connectivity with the ACC was observed in the reappraisal relative to the passive viewing and selective attention conditions. When comparing reappraisal to selective attention, functional connectivity was stronger for reappraisal in regions of left and right VLPFC, left dorsomedial PFC (DMPFC), right medial PFC, and posterior cingulate.

spans.text: Reappraisal > passive viewing: older adults |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

definition.value: Reappraisal was associated with stronger ACC connectivity than passive viewing in older adults.

value: Similar to younger adults, older adults showed significantly stronger connectivity with the ACC in the reappraisal condition compared with the passive viewing and selective attention conditions. Reappraisal was associated with stronger ACC connectivity than passive viewing in right DMPFC and left and right ventromedial PFC (VMPFC)/OFC.
